newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland eyes bank PBK public offering at turn Q3-Q4.
newsitem.headline: Poland eyes bank PBK public offering at turn Q3-Q4.

text.p: Poland's planned public offering of at least 51 percent of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) will be held at the turn of September and October, a deputy finance minister told the daily Rzeczpospolita in its Thursday edition.
"At least 51 percent of shares in Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA will go in a public offering at the turn of September and October," Karol Szwarc was quoted as saying.

Szwarc said that up to 19 percent more of PBK might go in a public offering later, up to 15 percent to employees, 10 percent to boost pension funds currently forming in Poland's social security reform and five percent to restitution claims.
The paper cited unofficial sources in saying that the latter offering of up to 19 percent of shares might go to a strategic investor or investors.
Szwarc would not say why the Polish government on Tuesday cancelled a tender for up to 65 pecent of PBK in which South Korea's Samsung Group and a Polish bank-insurance group had bid.
Polish Development Bank (PBR), a member of the Polish group, said on Wednesday that the group would mull buying shares in the new public offering.
The Polish group is also made up of Bank Przemyslowo- Handlowy SA (BPH), Kredyt Bank and insurer Warta.

Under the original privatisation plan only 15 percent of PBK was to be sold in a public offering, expected in the fourth quarter of this year, with 65 percent earmarked for a strategic investor or a consortium and the rest set aside for the bank's employees and a special reserve for restitution claims.

The decision on the choice of the strategic investor had been delayed for months and Samsung earlier this month accused the Polish government of favouring the Polish offer even though it was less attractive financially.
Warsaw-based PBK is one of Poland's leading retail banks. HSBC Investment Services SA, which advised the government on the bank's privatisation, has estimated its value at 1.2-1.6 billion zlotys.
